content.title: About
content.content: Oatmeal (regular or quick‑cooking) is prepared with water and added fat. Oats (Avena sativa) are a cereal grain cultivated in temperate regions. The flakes have a mild, slightly nutty flavor and a hearty texture that retains much of the grain’s fiber.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Oats are among the oldest cultivated crops, with evidence of use dating back over 5,000 years in Mesopotamia.
Quick‑cooking oats are pre‑steamed and cut thinner, which speeds up hydration.
Oats contain beta‑glucan, a soluble fiber known to help lower cholesterol levels.
In traditional Scottish cuisine, oats are used to make “porridge,” a thick stew of oats cooked in water or milk.
Oats are frequently used as a base for plant‑based milks and vegetarian burger patties.

items.title: Rich in beta‑glucan
items.content: Beta‑glucan helps reduce LDL cholesterol and supports healthy gut microbiota.

items.title: Source of complex carbs
items.content: Complex carbohydrates provide sustained energy and help maintain stable blood glucose levels.

items.title: Contains iron and magnesium
items.content: Iron is essential for hemoglobin formation, while magnesium supports muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Low in sugar
items.content: Prepared with water and no added sugar, oatmeal fits well into low‑sugar diets.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: The combination of fiber, antioxidants, and healthy fats contributes to heart health.

items.title: Oat allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience allergic reactions to oats or oat proteins.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Phytic acid can bind minerals and reduce their absorption; soaking or sprouting lowers its level.

items.title: Gluten cross‑contamination
items.content: Oats are often processed on the same equipment as wheat, so people with celiac disease should choose certified gluten‑free oats.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Oatmeal can be cooked as a hot porridge, blended into smoothies, used in baked goods, energy bars, or as a base for vegan “meat” alternatives. Adding a small amount of fat (butter, oil, cream) enhances flavor and improves absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store oatmeal in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life, keep it in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent fat oxidation.
